label: thm:cauchy-A
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:cauchy-A}
Let Assumption~\ref{asm:classical} hold with $n\ge 2$, let $\alpha\in{\mathbb R}$, and let $f\in C 
  \def#1{n} 
  \def0{0} 
  \ifx#10\else^{n}\fi
_{w_{\alpha},\infty}({\mathbb R}^d)$. Then
\[
u(t,x):=P_t f(x):={\mathbb{E}}_x[f(X_t)]
\]
is the unique classical solution of~\eqref{eq:Cauchy} within the class of polynomial growth
\[
\sup_{0\le t\le T}\sup_{x\in{\mathbb R}^d}\frac{|u(t,x)|}{w_\mu(x)}<\infty,
\qquad\text{for every }T>0,\quad \mu:=\max(\alpha,1),
\]
and, for every $k\in\{0,\dots,n\}$,
\[
\|\mathrm{D}^k u(t,x)\|\le \|P_t f\|_{C 
  \def#1{n} 
  \def0{0} 
  \ifx#10\else^{n}\fi
_{w_{\alpha}}}\,w_{\alpha-k}(x)\le e^{ct}\|f\|_{C 
  \def#1{n} 
  \def0{0} 
  \ifx#10\else^{n}\fi
_{w_{\alpha}}}\,w_{\alpha-k}(x).
\]
head: environment

label: asm:bounded_derivatives
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{asm:bounded_derivatives}
    Fix $n\in{\mathbb N}$. The coefficients satisfy
    \[
        b\in C^{n+1}_{\mathrm{loc}}({\mathbb R}^d;{\mathbb R}^d),
        \qquad
        \sigma\in C^{n+1}_{\mathrm{loc}}({\mathbb R}^d;{\mathbb R}^{d\times m}),
    \]
    and
    \[
        |b(x)|\le B_0(1+|x|),
        \qquad
        \|\sigma(x)\|\le S_0(1+|x|),
        \qquad x\in{\mathbb R}^d,
    \]
    and
    \[
        \sup_{x\in{\mathbb R}^d}\|\mathrm{D}^k b(x)\|\le \widetilde B,
        \qquad
        \sup_{x\in{\mathbb R}^d}\|\mathrm{D}^k \sigma(x)\|\le \widetilde S,
        \qquad k=1,\dots,n+1.
    \]

label: thm:cauchy-B
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:cauchy-B}
Let Assumption~\ref{asm:bounded_derivatives} hold with $n=2$, and let $f\in C 
  \def#1{2} 
  \def0{0} 
  \ifx#10\else^{2,\mathrm{bd}}\fi
_{w_2,\infty}({\mathbb R}^d)$. Consider the Cauchy problem
\[
\partial_t u(t,x)={\@fontswitch\relax\mathcal L} u(t,x),
\qquad
u(0,x)=f(x),
\]
where ${\@fontswitch\relax\mathcal L}$ is defined in~\eqref{eq:generator-def}. Then
\[
u(t,x)=P_t f(x)={\mathbb{E}}_x[f(X_t)]
\]
is the unique classical solution satisfying
\[
u\in C([0,\infty);C 
  \def#1{2} 
  \def0{0} 
  \ifx#10\else^{2,\mathrm{bd}}\fi
_{w_2,\infty}({\mathbb R}^d))
\cap
C^1([0,\infty);C 
  \def#1{0} 
  \def0{0} 
  \ifx#10\else^{0,\mathrm{bd}}\fi
_{w_2,\infty}({\mathbb R}^d)).
\]
Moreover, there exist $c,M\ge 0$, such that for every $t\ge 0$ and $x\in{\mathbb R}^d$,
\[
|u(t,x)|\le e^{ct}\|f\|_{C 
  \def#1{2} 
  \def0{0} 
  \ifx#10\else^{2,\mathrm{bd}}\fi
_{w_2}}\,w_2(x),
\qquad
\|\mathrm{D} u(t,x)\|\le e^{ct}\|f\|_{C 
  \def#1{2} 
  \def0{0} 
  \ifx#10\else^{2,\mathrm{bd}}\fi
_{w_2}},
\qquad
\|\mathrm{D}^2 u(t,x)\|\le \bigl(1+M t^{1/2}\bigr)e^{ct}\|f\|_{C 
  \def#1{2} 
  \def0{0} 
  \ifx#10\else^{2,\mathrm{bd}}\fi
_{w_2}}.
\]

label: ex:moments
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:moments}
Fix a multi-index $\gamma=(\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_d)\in{\mathbb N}_0^d$ of order $|\gamma|:=\gamma_1+\cdots+\gamma_d$, and set
\[
    f_\gamma(x):=x^\gamma=x_1^{\gamma_1}\cdots x_d^{\gamma_d}.
\]
For every \(n\in{\mathbb N}_0\), one has \(\|f_\gamma\|_{C 
  \def#1{n} 
  \def0{0} 
  \ifx#10\else^{n}\fi
_{w_{|\gamma|}}}<\infty\); moreover, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \(f_\gamma\inC 
  \def#1{n} 
  \def0{0} 
  \ifx#10\else^{n}\fi
_{w_{|\gamma|+\varepsilon},\infty}({\mathbb R}^d)\). The mixed moment map
\[
    u_\gamma(t,x):={\mathbb{E}}_x[X_t^\gamma]=P_tf_\gamma(x)
\]
is in $C^{n}_{\mathrm{loc}}({\mathbb R}^d)$, with all partial derivatives up to order $n$ of polynomial growth. Theorem~\ref{thm:cauchy-A}, applied with $\alpha=|\gamma|+\varepsilon$, gives the growth estimates of $u_\gamma$.
head: environment

label: ex:affine_polynomial
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:affine_polynomial}
Assume that
\[
    b(x)=b_0+Bx,\qquad
    \sigma_\ell(x)=s_\ell+S_\ell x,\qquad \ell=1,\dots,m,
\]
with $b_0,s_\ell\in{\mathbb R}^d$ and $B,S_\ell\in{\mathbb R}^{d\times d}$. Then Assumption~\ref{asm:classical} is satisfied for every $n$, and $a(x)=\sigma(x)\sigma(x)^\top$ has entries of degree at most two. If $\mathscr P_M$ denotes the polynomials on ${\mathbb R}^d$ of degree at most $M$, then
\[
    {\@fontswitch\relax\mathcal L}\mathscr P_M\subseteq \mathscr P_M .
\]
Indeed, $b\cdot\nabla p$ and $\operatorname{tr}(a\mathrm{D}^2p)$ have degree at most $M$. Thus, in Theorem~\ref{thm:cauchy-A} one may use weights $w_\alpha$ with $\alpha >M$.

label: prop:higher_jet_sde

title: Proof
body_md:
By the results of \cite[Theorem II.3.3]{Kunita1984SaintFlour}, cf.\ \cite[Theorem 3.4.2]{Kunita2019}, there exists a modification of $x \mapsto X_t(x)$ that is $C^r$, and the derivatives
\[
Y_t^{(j)}(x)=\mathrm{D}_x^j X_t(x), \qquad j=1,\dots,r,
\]
are adapted and continuous in $t$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                      

Fix $v_1,\dots,v_r\in {\mathbb R}^d$. For every $s\ge0$ and almost every $\omega$, the map
\[
x \longmapsto X_s(x,\omega)
\]
is of class $C^r$, while $b$ and $\sigma_\ell$ are of class $C^r$. We may therefore apply Proposition 3.1 of \cite{Licht2024} pathwise to the compositions $b\circ X_s(\cdot,\omega)$ and $\sigma_\ell\circ X_s(\cdot,\omega)$. This yields \eqref{eq:Faa_di_Bruno_b} and \eqref{eq:Faa_di_Bruno_sigma}.

Approximating the derivatives by finite differences as in \cite[\ifmmode\mathsection\else\textsection\fi3.4]{Kunita2019} gives \eqref{eq:higher-jet}.

label: lemm:ito_gronwall
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemm:ito_gronwall}
Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space (in our applications \(E={\mathbb R}^d\) or \(E=\mathfrak L_r({\mathbb R}^d,{\mathbb R}^d)\) with the Hilbert--Schmidt inner product, or a tensor product of these). Let \(p\ge2\), and let \(M_t\in E\) be an It\^o process satisfying
\[
    dM_t=\bigl(\mathfrak A_tM_t+H_t\bigr)\,dt+\sum_{\ell=1}^m\bigl(\mathfrak B_{\ell,t}M_t+K_{\ell,t}\bigr)\,dW_t^\ell,\qquad M_0\in E,
\]
with adapted coefficients \(\mathfrak A_t,\mathfrak B_{\ell,t}:E\to E\) satisfying \(\|\mathfrak A_t\|+\sum_\ell\|\mathfrak B_{\ell,t}\|\le L\), and adapted processes \(H_t,K_{\ell,t}\in E\) with
\[
    {\mathbb{E}}|H_s|^p+\sum_{\ell=1}^m{\mathbb{E}}|K_{\ell,s}|^p\le\varphi(s),\qquad 0\le s\le T,
\]
for some non-decreasing, locally integrable \(\varphi:[0,T]\to[0,\infty)\). Then there is a constant \(C>0\) such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ito_gronwall}
    {\mathbb{E}}|M_t|^p\le\Bigl({\mathbb{E}}|M_0|^p+\int_0^t\varphi(s)\,ds\Bigr)e^{Ct},\qquad 0\le t\le T.
\end{equation}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix \(\varepsilon\in(0,1]\) and set \(V_t^\varepsilon:=(\varepsilon+|M_t|^2)^{p/2}\), \(\tau_N^\varepsilon:=\inf\{t:V_t^\varepsilon\ge N\}\). It\^o's formula applied to the smooth function \(z\mapsto(\varepsilon+|z|^2)^{p/2}\), combined with \(\|\mathfrak A_t\|+\sum_\ell\|\mathfrak B_{\ell,t}\|\le L\) and Young's inequality, yields
\[
    {\mathbb{E}} V_{t\wedge\tau_N^\varepsilon}^\varepsilon\le{\mathbb{E}} V_0^\varepsilon+C\int_0^t\bigl({\mathbb{E}} V_{s\wedge\tau_N^\varepsilon}^\varepsilon+\varphi(s)\bigr)\,ds,
\]
where \(C>0\). Gronwall's inequality gives
\({\mathbb{E}} V_{t\wedge\tau_N^\varepsilon}^\varepsilon\le\bigl({\mathbb{E}} V_0^\varepsilon+\int_0^t\varphi(s)\,ds\bigr)e^{Ct}\).
Letting \(N\to\infty\) (Fatou) and then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) yields \eqref{eq:ito_gronwall}.
head: environment

label: lemm:multi_d_1st
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: eq:Mtv_SDE
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix \(v\in{\mathbb R}^d\) and set \(M_t:=Y_tv\). By Proposition~\ref{prop:higher_jet_sde}, we have the SDE
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Mtv_SDE}
    M_t=v+\int_0^t \mathrm{D} b(X_s)M_s\,ds+\sum_{\ell=1}^m\int_0^t\mathrm{D}\sigma_\ell(X_s)M_s\,dW_s^\ell .
\end{equation}

\emph{Case \(p\ge2\).} Fix \(\varepsilon\in(0,1]\) and let \(f_\varepsilon(z):=(\varepsilon+|z|^2)^{p/2}\). Then \(f_\varepsilon\in C^2({\mathbb R}^d)\) with
\[
    \nabla f_\varepsilon(z)=p(\varepsilon+|z|^2)^{p/2-1}\,z,\qquad
    \mathrm{D}^2 f_\varepsilon(z)=p(\varepsilon+|z|^2)^{p/2-1}I_d+p(p-2)(\varepsilon+|z|^2)^{p/2-2}\,zz^\top .
\]
By It\^o's formula applied to \eqref{eq:Mtv_SDE}, the drift of \(f_\varepsilon(M_t)\) is the sum of the first-order term
\[
    \nabla f_\varepsilon(M_s)\cdot\mathrm{D} b(X_s)M_s
    \le p(\varepsilon+|M_s|^2)^{p/2-1}\|\mathrm{D} b(X_s)\||M_s|^2
    \le pB_1f_\varepsilon(M_s)
\]
and the second-order term
\[
    \tfrac12\sum_{\ell=1}^m\mathrm{D}^2 f_\varepsilon(M_s)\bigl[\mathrm{D}\sigma_\ell(X_s)M_s,\mathrm{D}\sigma_\ell(X_s)M_s\bigr]
    \le \tfrac{p(p-1)}{2}S_1^2 f_\varepsilon(M_s);
\]
hence this drift is at most \(c\,f_\varepsilon(M_s)\) with \(c:=pB_1+\tfrac{p(p-1)}{2}S_1^2\). Set \(\tau_N:=\inf\{t\ge0:f_\varepsilon(M_t)\ge N\}\); on \([0,\tau_N]\) the It\^o stochastic integral has bounded integrand, hence is a true martingale, and taking expectations gives
\[
    {\mathbb{E}} f_\varepsilon(M_{t\wedge\tau_N})\le f_\varepsilon(v)+c\int_0^t{\mathbb{E}} f_\varepsilon(M_{s\wedge\tau_N})\,ds.
\]
Gronwall's lemma gives \({\mathbb{E}} f_\varepsilon(M_{t\wedge\tau_N})\le(\varepsilon+|v|^2)^{p/2}e^{ct}\). Fatou's lemma and monotone convergence yield \({\mathbb{E}}|M_t|^p\le|v|^p e^{ct}\).

\emph{Case \(0<p<2\).} The map \(x\mapsto x^{p/2}\) is concave on \([0,\infty)\), so Jensen's inequality gives
\[
    {\mathbb{E}}|M_t|^p={\mathbb{E}}\bigl[(|M_t|^2)^{p/2}\bigr]\le({\mathbb{E}}|M_t|^2)^{p/2}\le|v|^p e^{c_2pt/2}.
\]
Hence \eqref{eq:multi_1st} holds with \(c=\tfrac{p}{2}(2B_1+S_1^2)\).

label: prop:multid_bounded_derivatives
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{prop:multid_bounded_derivatives}
Let Assumption \ref{asm:bounded_derivatives} hold with $n\ge2$. Let $r\in\{2,\dots,n\}$ and $p>0$. Then there exists a constant $c_{r,p}>0$ such that
\[
\sup_{x\in{\mathbb R}^d}\sup_{|v_1|,\dots,|v_r|\le1}
{\mathbb{E}}_x \big|Y_t^{(r)}(x)[v_1,\dots,v_r]\big|^p
\le c_{r,p}\bigl(e^{c_{r,p} t}-1\bigr).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For \(j\ge1\), write
\[
\widetilde M_{j,p}(t):=\sup_{x\in{\mathbb R}^d}\sup_{|v_1|,\dots,|v_j|\le1}{\mathbb{E}}_x\big|Y_t^{(j)}(x)[v_1,\dots,v_j]\big|^p .
\]
The case \(j=1\) is Proposition~\ref{lemm:multi_d_1st}, which gives \(\widetilde M_{1,p}(t)\le e^{ct}\). The case \(0<p<2\) follows from \(p\ge2\) by the H\"older inequality, so it suffices to take \(p\ge2\). Fix \(r\in\{2,\dots,n\}\) and assume the bound for orders \(<r\). Set \(U_t^{(r)}:=Y_t^{(r)}(x)[v_1,\dots,v_r]\) with \(|v_i|\le1\). Under Assumption~\ref{asm:bounded_derivatives}, \(\|\mathrm{D}^qb\|+\max_\ell\|\mathrm{D}^q\sigma_\ell\|\le c\) uniformly for \(q=1,\dots,r\), so \eqref{eq:Yr_linear_rhs} puts \(U_t^{(r)}\) in the form of Lemma~\ref{lemm:ito_gronwall} with bounded linear coefficients and additional terms \(F_s^{(r)}, G_{\ell,s}^{(r)}\). For a partition with \(q\ge2\) blocks, the H\"older inequality and the hypothesis of induction give
\[
    {\mathbb{E}}_x\big|\mathrm{D}^qb(X_s)[Y_s^{(|B_1|)}[v_{B_1}],\dots,Y_s^{(|B_q|)}[v_{B_q}]]\big|^p\le c\,e^{cs}.
\]
Summing over the partitions in \eqref{eq:Fr_def} and \eqref{eq:Gr_def} gives
\[
    {\mathbb{E}}_x|F_s^{(r)}[v]|^p+\sum_\ell{\mathbb{E}}_x|G_{\ell,s}^{(r)}[v]|^p\le c\,e^{cs} .
\]
Lemma~\ref{lemm:ito_gronwall} with \(U_0^{(r)}=0\) and \(\varphi(s)=c\,e^{cs}\) yields \(\widetilde M_{r,p}(t)\le c(e^{ct}-1)\).

label: lemm:normalized_Z_sde
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The equation \eqref{eq:normalized_Z_sde} follows by applying It\^o's product rule to \(w_{r-1}(X_t)Y_t^{(r)}\) and using \eqref{eq:Yr_linear_rhs}. Since
\[
    dw_{r-1}(X_t)={\@fontswitch\relax\mathcal L} w_{r-1}(X_t)\,dt+\sum_{\ell=1}^m\nabla w_{r-1}(X_t)\sigma_\ell(X_t)\,dW_t^\ell,
\]
the quadratic covariation between \(w_{r-1}(X_t)\) and \(Y_t^{(r)}\) contributes
\[
    \sum_{\ell=1}^m\bigl(\nabla w_{r-1}(X_t)\sigma_\ell(X_t)\bigr)\bigl(\mathrm{D}\sigma_\ell(X_t)Y_t^{(r)}+G_{\ell,t}^{(r)}\bigr)\,dt.
\]
Collecting the parts linear in \(Y_t^{(r)}=w_{1-r}(X_t)Z_t^{(r)}\) gives the displayed coefficients \(\mathfrak A_t^{(r)}\) and \(\mathfrak B_{\ell,t}^{(r)}\), while what remains is precisely \(\widehat F_t^{(r)}\) and \(\widehat G_{\ell,t}^{(r)}\).

The boundedness of \(\mathfrak A_t^{(r)}\) and \(\mathfrak B_{\ell,t}^{(r)}\) follows from
\[
    \frac{|{\@fontswitch\relax\mathcal L} w_{r-1}(y)|}{w_{r-1}(y)}+\sum_{\ell=1}^m\frac{|\nabla w_{r-1}(y)\sigma_\ell(y)|}{w_{r-1}(y)}+\|\mathrm{D} b(y)\|+\sum_{\ell=1}^m\|\mathrm{D}\sigma_\ell(y)\|\le C,
\]
which is a direct consequence of Assumption \ref{asm:classical} and the elementary bounds \(|\nabla w_{r-1}|\le Cw_{r-1}w_{-1}\), \(\|\mathrm{D}^2w_{r-1}\|\le Cw_{r-1}w_{-2}\).

For \eqref{eq:normalized_Z_rhs_bound}, consider a summand of \(w_{r-1}(X_t)F_t^{(r)}\) for a partition \(\pi=\{B_1,\dots,B_q\}\) with \(q\ge2\), namely
\[
    w_{r-1}(X_t)\,\mathrm{D}^q b(X_t)\bigl[Y_t^{(|B_1|)}[v_{B_1}],\dots,Y_t^{(|B_q|)}[v_{B_q}]\bigr].
\]
Write each \(Y_t^{(|B_j|)}=w_{1-|B_j|}(X_t)Z_t^{(|B_j|)}\) and use \(\|\mathrm{D}^q b(X_t)\|\le Cw_{1-q}(X_t)\) (Assumption~\ref{asm:classical}). The summand has the weight 
\[
    w_{r-1}(X_t)\,w_{1-q}(X_t)\prod_{j=1}^qw_{1-|B_j|}(X_t)=w_0(X_t)=1,
\]
the exponents summing to \((r-1)+(1-q)+\sum_{j=1}^q(1-|B_j|)=0\) since \(\sum_j|B_j|=r\). Here \(w_{r-1}\) is the normalization, \(w_{1-q}\) is the bound on \(\mathrm{D}^q b\), and each \(w_{1-|B_j|}\) normalizes the jet \(Y_t^{(|B_j|)}\); their exact cancellation to \(w_0=1\) is what leaves \(\widehat F_t^{(r)}\) a bounded combination of the normalized derivatives \(Z_t^{(|B_j|)}\). The summands of \(w_{r-1}G_\ell^{(r)}\) are treated identically, with \(\sigma_\ell\) in place of \(b\).

The remaining term in the formula for \(\widehat F_t^{(r)}\), namely \((\nabla w_{r-1}(X_t)\sigma_\ell(X_t))\,G_{\ell,t}^{(r)}\), is treated in a similar way. Summing over the partitions gives \eqref{eq:normalized_Z_rhs_bound}.

label: lemm:multid
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By induction on \(r\). The case \(r=1\) is Proposition~\ref{lemm:multi_d_1st}. Take \(p\ge2\) (\(0<p<2\) follows by the H\"older inequality), fix \(r\ge2\) and \(|v_i|\le1\).

Set \(U_t:=Y_t^{(r)}[v_1,\dots,v_r]\). The SDE \eqref{eq:Yr_linear_rhs} fits Lemma~\ref{lemm:ito_gronwall} with linear coefficients \(\mathrm{D} b(X_t),\mathrm{D}\sigma_\ell(X_t)\), bounded by Assumption~\ref{asm:classical}, and additional terms \(F_s^{(r)},G_{\ell,s}^{(r)}\). Fix a partition \(\pi=\{B_1,\dots,B_q\}\) with \(q\ge2\); Assumption~\ref{asm:classical} gives \(\|\mathrm{D}^qb(X_s)\|\le c\,w_{1-q}(X_s)\). Apply the H\"older inequality at exponent \(p(q+1)\) to
\[
    R_{\pi,s}:=\mathrm{D}^qb(X_s)[Y_s^{(|B_1|)}[v_{B_1}],\dots,Y_s^{(|B_q|)}[v_{B_q}]].
\]
Using Lemma~\ref{lemm:invariant} (\({\mathbb{E}}_xw_{1-q}(X_s)^{p(q+1)}\le c\,e^{cs}w_{1-q}(x)^{p(q+1)}\)) and the hypothesis of induction, we obtain
\[
    {\mathbb{E}}_x|R_{\pi,s}|^p\le c\,e^{cs}\,w_{1-q}(x)^p\prod_j w_{1-|B_j|}(x)^p
    =c\,e^{cs}\,w_{1-r}(x)^p,
\]
since \(\sum_j|B_j|=r\). Summing in \eqref{eq:Fr_def}, \eqref{eq:Gr_def} and applying Lemma~\ref{lemm:ito_gronwall} with \(U_0=0\), \(\varphi(s)=c\,e^{cs}w_{1-r}(x)^p\) gives \eqref{eq:multi_higher}.

The inequality \eqref{eq:higher_Z} is proven similarly, thanks to Lemma~\ref{lemm:normalized_Z_sde} and Lemma~\ref{lemm:ito_gronwall}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Set \(h:=\#\{i:r_i=\max_ir_i\}\); splitting the indices into \(h\) groups with one factor of maximal order each, factoring \(R_t^\beta=\prod_{a=1}^hR_t^{\beta/h}\), and replacing \(p\) by \(ph\) reduces to \(h=1\).

\emph{Case \(\max_ir_i=1\).} Here \(Z^{(1)}=Y^{(1)}\); the H\"older inequality on the \(k+1\) factors \(R_t^\beta,Z_t^{(1)}[v_1],\dots,Z_t^{(1)}[v_k]\), Lemma~\ref{lemm:invariant}, and Proposition~\ref{lemm:multi_d_1st} give \(Ce^{Ct}\).

\emph{Case \(\max_ir_i=r_1\ge2\)} (assuming the claim for smaller maximal order). By It\^o's formula, \(R_t^\beta\) satisfies a linear SDE with coefficients bounded by Assumption~\ref{asm:classical}. The It\^o product rule and Lemma~\ref{lemm:normalized_Z_sde} then cast \(R_t^\beta U_t\) into the form of Lemma~\ref{lemm:ito_gronwall}. The hypothesis of induction (or Case~1 if every factor has order one) bounds \({\mathbb{E}}_x|R^\beta\widetilde U|^p\) by \(Ce^{Cs}\). Since \(R_0^\beta U_0=0\), Lemma~\ref{lemm:ito_gronwall} gives the bound.

label: lem:weighted_product_expectation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:weighted_product_expectation}
Let \(n\in{\mathbb N}\), let Assumption~\ref{asm:classical} hold, let \(a\in\{2,\dots,n\}\), let \(q\in{\mathbb N}\) satisfy \(a+q-1\le n\), and let \(\beta\in{\mathbb R}\). For unit vectors \(v_1,\dots,v_a,u_1,\dots,u_{q-1}\in{\mathbb R}^d\), set
\[
    V_t:=R_t^\beta Z_t^{(a)}[v_1,\dots,v_a]\otimes\bigotimes_{j=1}^{q-1}Z_t^{(1)}[u_j],
\]
with the empty tensor product interpreted as the scalar \(1\). Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted_product_expectation}
    \left|{\mathbb{E}}_x V_t\right|\le C(e^{Ct}-1),
    \qquad t\ge0,
\end{equation}
for some \(C>0\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since \(Z_0^{(a)}=0\) for \(a\ge2\) by Lemma~\ref{lemm:normalized_Z_sde}, \(V_0=0\). The It\^o product rule, applied as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:weighted_product_multi}, gives an SDE
\[
    dV_t=\bigl(\mathfrak A_t V_t+\widetilde F_t\bigr)\,dt+\sum_\ell\bigl(\mathfrak B_{\ell,t} V_t+\widetilde G_{\ell,t}\bigr)\,dW_t^\ell,
\]
with uniformly bounded linear coefficients \(\mathfrak A_t,\mathfrak B_{\ell,t}\). The terms \(\widetilde F_t,\widetilde G_{\ell,t}\) come from the additional term in the SDE for \(Z^{(a)}\) (Lemma~\ref{lemm:normalized_Z_sde}); each has the form of \(V_t\) with the factor \(Z^{(a)}\) replaced by a product \(Z^{(s_1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes Z^{(s_h)}\) with \(h\ge2\), \(s_i<a\), and \(\sum_i s_i=a\). Taking expectations eliminates the stochastic integrals, so
\[
    |{\mathbb{E}}_x V_t|
    \le \int_0^t\|\mathfrak A_s\|\,{\mathbb{E}}_x|V_s|\,ds+\int_0^t {\mathbb{E}}_x|\widetilde F_s|\,ds.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:weighted_product_multi} applied to \(V_s\) (max-order \(a\ge2\)) gives \({\mathbb{E}}_x|V_s|\le C(e^{Cs}-1)^{1/2}\); applied to each summand of \(\widetilde F_s\), whose index of maximal order is \(<a\), it gives \({\mathbb{E}}_x|\widetilde F_s|\le Ce^{Cs}\). Hence
\[
    |{\mathbb{E}}_x V_t|\le C\int_0^t (e^{Cs}-1)^{1/2}\,ds+C\int_0^t e^{Cs}\,ds
    \le C(e^{Ct}-1),
\]
where the last step uses \(\int_0^t(e^{Cs}-1)^{1/2}\,ds\le C(e^{Ct}-1)\), bounding the integrand by \((Cs)^{1/2}\) for small \(s\) and by \(e^{Cs/2}\) for large \(s\).

Put \(\beta=\alpha-r\) and \(R_t^\beta=w_\beta(X_t)/w_\beta(x)\). If at least two blocks of \(\pi\) have size at least two, relabel them as \(B_1\) and \(B_2\), set \(U_j:=Z_t^{(s_j)}[v_{B_j}]\), and split the remaining indices \(\{3,\dots,q\}\) into two disjoint sets \(I\) and \(I^c\). Since \(R_t^\beta=R_t^{\beta/2}R_t^{\beta/2}\), Cauchy's inequality gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\left|
{\mathbb{E}}_x\left[
R_t^\beta J_qf(X_t)[U_1,\dots,U_q]
\right]\right|  \\
&\qquad\le
\|f\|_{C

_{w_{\alpha}}}
\left({\mathbb{E}}_x\left|R_t^{\beta/2}U_1\otimes\bigotimes_{j\in I}U_j\right|^2\right)^{1/2}
\left({\mathbb{E}}_x\left|R_t^{\beta/2}U_2\otimes\bigotimes_{j\in I^c}U_j\right|^2\right)^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Each \(L^2\)-norm contains one normalized derivative of higher order, hence is bounded by \(C(e^{Ct}-1)^{1/2}\) by Lemma~\ref{lem:weighted_product_multi}, yielding the stated bound.

If exactly one block has size \(a\ge2\) and the rest are singletons, relabel so that \(s_1=a\) and write

    J_qf(X_t)=J_qf(x)+\bigl(J_qf(X_t)-J_qf(x)\bigr).
\]
The first term is estimated by Lemma \ref{lem:weighted_product_expectation}. For the second term, Cauchy's inequality, Lemma \ref{lem:J_increment_stochastic}, and Lemma \ref{lem:weighted_product_multi} yield
\[
\begin{aligned}

R_t^\beta\|J_qf(X_t)-J_qf(x)\|
|Z_t^{(a)}[v_{B_1}]|
\prod_{j=2}^q|Z_t^{(1)}[v_{B_j}]|
\right]  \\
&\qquad\le
\left({\mathbb{E}}_x\|J_qf(X_t)-J_qf(x)\|^2\right)^{1/2}

&\qquad\le C(e^{Ct}-1)\|f\|_{C

_{w_{\alpha}}}.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:diff_under_expectation}
Let \(n\in{\mathbb N}\), \(\alpha\in{\mathbb R}\), let Assumption~\ref{asm:classical} hold, and \(f\inC 
  \def#1{n} 
  \def0{0} 
  \ifx#10\else^{n}\fi
_{w_{\alpha}}({\mathbb R}^d)\). Then \(P_tf\inC^{n}_{\mathrm{loc}}({\mathbb R}^d)\) and, for every \(r\in\{1,\dots,n\}\),
\[
\mathrm{D}^r P_t f(x)[v_1,\dots,v_r]={\mathbb{E}}_x\Big[
\sum_{k=1}^r \sum_{\pi=\{B_1,\dots,B_k\}\in \mathcal P(r,k)}
\mathrm{D}^k f(X_t(x))
\big[
Y_t^{(|B_1|)}(x)[v_{B_1}],
\dots,
Y_t^{(|B_k|)}(x)[v_{B_k}]
\big]
\Big].
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a compact \(K\subset{\mathbb R}^d\), \(r\le n\), a partition \(\pi=\{B_1,\dots,B_k\}\in\mathcal P(r,k)\), \(s_j:=|B_j|\), and unit vectors \(v_1,\dots,v_r\). With \(J_kf=w_{k-\alpha}\mathrm{D}^kf\) and \(Z_t^{(s_j)}=w_{s_j-1}(X_t)Y_t^{(s_j)}\), the identity \(\sum_js_j=r\) gives
\[
\mathrm{D}^kf(X_t)\big[Y_t^{(s_1)}[v_{B_1}],\dots,Y_t^{(s_k)}[v_{B_k}]\big]
=w_{\alpha-r}(x)\,\frac{w_{\alpha-r}(X_t)}{w_{\alpha-r}(x)}\,J_kf(X_t)\big[Z_t^{(s_1)}[v_{B_1}],\dots,Z_t^{(s_k)}[v_{B_k}]\big].
\]
With \(\|J_kf\|_\infty\le\|f\|_{C 
  \def#1{n} 
  \def0{0} 
  \ifx#10\else^{n}\fi
_{w_{\alpha}}}\) and \(w_{\alpha-r}\) bounded on \(K\), Lemma~\ref{lem:weighted_product_multi} yields
\[
\sup_{x\in K}{\mathbb{E}}_x\big|\mathrm{D}^kf(X_t)[Y_t^{(s_1)}[v_{B_1}],\dots,Y_t^{(s_k)}[v_{B_k}]]\big|^p<\infty
\qquad\text{for some }p>1.
\]
Standard arguments using this local \(L^p\)-bound (uniform integrability and finite-difference approximation, cf.\ \cite[\ifmmode\mathsection\else\textsection\fi3.4]{Kunita2019}) give the displayed formula and continuity of \(\mathrm{D}^rP_tf\).

label: lem:weighted_compact_core
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:weighted_compact_core}
Let \(N\in{\mathbb N}_0\), suppose Assumption~\ref{asm:classical} is satisfied for some integer \(n\ge N\), and let \(g\in C_c^\infty({\mathbb R}^d)\). Then, for every compact \(K\subset{\mathbb R}^d\) and every \(0\le m\le N\),
\[
    \sup_{x\in K}\frac{\|\mathrm{D}^mP_tg(x)-\mathrm{D}^mg(x)\|}{w_{\alpha-m}(x)}\to0,
    \qquad t\downarrow0.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
On \(K\) the weights are bounded above and below, so it suffices to control \(\sup_{x\in K}\|\mathrm{D}^mP_tg(x)-\mathrm{D}^mg(x)\|\); the case \(m=0\) is the Feller property. Fix \(1\le m\le N\) and \(|v_i|\le1\), and split \(\mathrm{D}^mP_tg[v]\) by Lemma~\ref{lem:diff_under_expectation} into the singleton part \(S_t(x)[v]={\mathbb{E}}_x[\mathrm{D}^mg(X_t)[Y_t^{(1)}v_1,\dots,Y_t^{(1)}v_m]]\) and the non-singleton remainder \(R_t(x)[v]\). Each summand of \(R_t\) carries a factor \(Y_t^{(a)}\) with \(a\ge2\); the H\"older inequality together with Proposition~\ref{lemm:multi_d_1st} and Lemma~\ref{lemm:multid} gives \(\sup_{x\in K}\|R_t(x)\|\le C_g(e^{ct}-1)^{1/p}e^{ct}\to0\) for some \(p>1\). For the singleton part, expanding \(\bigotimes_i(I+(Y_t^{(1)}-I))v_i\) gives
\[
    S_t(x)[v]-\mathrm{D}^mg(x)[v]=\bigl({\mathbb{E}}_x[\mathrm{D}^mg(X_t)[v]]-\mathrm{D}^mg(x)[v]\bigr)+B_t(x)[v],
\]
where \(B_t\) collects the \(2^m-1\) terms with at least one factor \(Y_t^{(1)}-I\). The first difference tends to zero uniformly on \(K\) because each component of \(\mathrm{D}^mg\) lies in \(C_\infty({\mathbb R}^d)\), while \(|B_t(x)[v]|\le C_g{\mathbb{E}}_x[(1+\|Y_t^{(1)}\|^{m-1})\|Y_t^{(1)}-I\|]\). Since \(Y_t^{(1)}-I\) starts from zero, the Burkholder--Davis--Gundy inequality and Proposition~\ref{lemm:multi_d_1st} give \(\sup_{x\in K}{\mathbb{E}}_x\|Y_t^{(1)}-I\|^p\le C_Kt^{p/2}\) for \(0<t\le1\), so \(B_t\to0\) and \(\sup_{x\in K}\|S_t(x)-\mathrm{D}^mg(x)\|\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\).

body_md:
The case \(r=0\) is Proposition~\ref{theo:strongly_continuous} with \(\alpha=2\). For \(1\le r\le N\), the Fa\`a di Bruno formula of Lemma~\ref{lem:diff_under_expectation_bounded_derivatives} yields the singleton/non-singleton decomposition of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:weighted_compact_core}:
\[
    \mathrm{D}^rP_tg-\mathrm{D}^rg=R_t+\bigl({\mathbb{E}}[\mathrm{D}^rg(X_t)]-\mathrm{D}^rg\bigr)+B_t,
\]
where \(B_t\) collects the \(2^r-1\) non-identity terms in \(\bigotimes_i(I+(Y_t^{(1)}-I))v_i\). Under Assumption~\ref{asm:bounded_derivatives}, the moments from Proposition~\ref{lemm:multi_d_1st} and Lemma~\ref{prop:multid_bounded_derivatives} are uniform in \(x\). The three bounds used in Lemma~\ref{lem:weighted_compact_core} transfer: the H\"older inequality bounds \(\|R_t\|_\infty\); \(\mathrm{D}^rg\in C_\infty\) controls the continuity difference; and Burkholder--Davis--Gundy with Proposition~\ref{lemm:multi_d_1st} bounds \(|B_t(x)|\) by \(C_g{\mathbb{E}}_x[(1+\|Y_t^{(1)}\|^{r-1})\|Y_t^{(1)}-I\|]\). Together they give \(\sup_x\|\mathrm{D}^rP_tg(x)-\mathrm{D}^rg(x)\|\to0\).

For \(P_tg\inC 
  \def#1{N} 
  \def0{0} 
  \ifx#10\else^{N,\mathrm{bd}}\fi
_{w_2,\infty}\), the H\"older inequality dominates each Fa\`a di Bruno summand containing \(\mathrm{D}^qg(X_t)\) by \(C_g(P_t\varphi(x))^\theta\), \(\theta\in(0,1)\), where \(\varphi\in C_c^\infty({\mathbb R}^d)\) equals \(1\) on \(\operatorname{supp}\mathrm{D}^qg\); \(P_t\varphi\in C_\infty({\mathbb R}^d)\) by Lemma~\ref{lemm:weighted_feller}.
